patterns.pattern_name: JWT-based Authentication with Access and Refresh Tokens

permissions: CUSTOMER: access to public endpoints only
ADMIN: access to all endpoints including /api/v1/admin/**

data_items.flow_summary: Passwords are hashed with BCrypt before storage. Transmitted over HTTPS during registration and login. Never returned in API responses.

locations: access_token table (MySQL) - token field (plain text, signed)
refresh_token table (MySQL) - token field (plain text, signed)
data_items.flow_summary: JWT tokens are generated on login, stored in database with expiration and revocation flags. Tokens are signed with HS256 but not encrypted at rest. Transmitted over HTTPS.

locations: users table (MySQL) - email field (plain text, unique)
action_history table (MySQL) - userEmail, updateByAdminEmail fields (plain text)
data_items.flow_summary: Email addresses are stored in plain text, used for authentication and audit logging. Transmitted over HTTPS. Included in email notifications sent via Gmail SMTP.

locations: users table (MySQL) - firstname, lastname fields (plain text)
data_items.flow_summary: User names are stored in plain text, included in JWT token payload, and used in email notifications. Transmitted over HTTPS.

data_items.data_type: Audit and Compliance Data - Action History
data_items.flow_summary: Admin actions on user accounts are logged with timestamps, admin attribution, and action details. Stored in plain text. Accessible only to admins via /api/v1/admin/action-history endpoint.
OneView API credentials (username and password) are hardcoded in source code. Used to authenticate with external OneView API over HTTPS.
Gmail SMTP credentials (username and app password) are stored in plain text in configuration file. Used to send email notifications over SMTP/SSL.

MySQL database credentials (username and password) are stored in plain text in configuration file. Used to connect to AWS RDS MySQL database. SSL/TLS not explicitly configured for database connection.

recommendations.recommendation: Immediately remove hardcoded OneView API credentials from source code and store in environment variables or AWS Secrets Manager
recommendations.rationale: Hardcoded credentials in source code are a critical security vulnerability. Anyone with repository access can view and misuse these credentials.
recommendations.standard_alignment: OWASP Top 10 (A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures), CWE-798 (Use of Hard-coded Credentials)

recommendations.recommendation: Move all credentials (database, SMTP, JWT secrets) from application-dev.properties to environment variables or AWS Secrets Manager
recommendations.rationale: Configuration files with plain text credentials can be accidentally committed to version control or exposed through misconfigured deployments.
recommendations.standard_alignment: OWASP Top 10 (A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures), NIST SP 800-53 (IA-5)

recommendations.recommendation: Enable SSL/TLS for MySQL database connections by adding SSL parameters to JDBC URL
recommendations.rationale: Database traffic may be transmitted in plain text without SSL/TLS, exposing sensitive data to network sniffing.
recommendations.standard_alignment: OWASP Top 10 (A02:2021 – Cryptographic Failures), PCI DSS 4.1

recommendations.recommendation: Implement rate limiting on authentication endpoints (/login, /register) to prevent brute force attacks
recommendations.rationale: Without rate limiting, authentication endpoints are vulnerable to brute force attacks, credential stuffing, and denial of service.
recommendations.standard_alignment: OWASP Top 10 (A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures), NIST SP 800-63B

recommendations.recommendation: Implement account lockout mechanism after failed login attempts
recommendations.rationale: Account lockout prevents brute force attacks by temporarily disabling accounts after multiple failed login attempts.
recommendations.standard_alignment: OWASP Top 10 (A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures), NIST SP 800-63B

recommendations.recommendation: Implement comprehensive audit logging for all authentication events (successful and failed logins)
recommendations.rationale: Audit logging is essential for detecting and responding to security incidents, brute force attacks, and unauthorized access attempts.

recommendations.recommendation: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users, especially admin accounts
recommendations.rationale: MFA significantly reduces the risk of account compromise from credential theft and phishing attacks.

recommendations.recommendation: Implement GDPR data subject rights endpoints (right to access, rectification, erasure, data portability)
recommendations.rationale: GDPR compliance requires providing data subjects with mechanisms to exercise their rights over their personal data.

recommendations.recommendation: Consider encrypting JWT tokens at rest in database
recommendations.rationale: While JWT tokens are signed, encrypting them at rest provides an additional layer of protection against database compromise.

recommendations.recommendation: Implement data retention and deletion policies for audit logs and user data
recommendations.rationale: Data retention policies are required for GDPR compliance and help minimize data exposure risk.

smells.description: OneView API credentials (username and password) are hardcoded in OneViewServiceImpl.java source code
Database and SMTP credentials stored in plain text in application-dev.properties
MySQL database connection does not explicitly configure SSL/TLS encryption
evidence: No SSL configuration in JDBC URL

smells.description: Authentication endpoints (login, register) lack rate limiting
evidence: No rate limiting annotations or configuration detected

smells.description: No account lockout mechanism after failed login attempts
evidence: No failed login attempt tracking or lockout logic detected

smells.smell_type: No Audit Logging for Authentication Events
smells.description: Failed login attempts and authentication events are not logged for security monitoring
evidence: No explicit logging of failed login attempts

smells.description: No MFA implementation for user authentication
evidence: No MFA-related code detected in security package

smells.description: CORS configuration may allow all origins
evidence: Permissive CORS configuration detected in repository summary

limits_or_unknowns: HTTPS enforcement not explicitly verified in code; assumed based on production deployment context
Network security controls (firewalls, security groups) not visible in application code
AWS RDS encryption at rest configuration not visible in application code
Secrets manager integration not detected; may be configured at deployment level
Rate limiting may be implemented at API gateway level (not visible in application code)
MFA implementation may be planned but not yet implemented
CORS configuration details not fully visible; marked as low confidence
